newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to cut steel imports, boost local output.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to cut steel imports, boost local output.

text.p: Vietnam plans to halve steel imports this year and increase local production to prevent another overhang of stock and protect local industry, state-owned Vietnam Steel Corporation (VSC) said on Thursday.
A VSC official, who declined to be named, said this year's target for domestic output of steel was 1.2 million tonnes, up from 800,000 last year.
Imports would be limited to 400,000 tonnes, half of last year's total, he said.
Local press reports had put the ceiling on this year's imports even lower at 300,000 tonnes and said firms with a foreign partner would no longer be exempt from tax on steel they import.

The daily Vietnam News quoted VSC's General Director, Ho Nghia Dung, as saying there should be a 10 percent increase in the tax paid by other firms on their steel imports to "protect home-made goods and increase contributions to state coffers".
Dung, labelling 1996 as "the darkest time for the steel industry", said local steel plants had operated at only 80-90 percent of capacity.

Production was depressed by a heavy flow of cheap steel from abroad, which created a glut in the domestic market. More than 400,000 tonnes of steel is sitting in store houses, over half of it stock held by VSC.
The VSC official said Vietnam was aiming to produce between 2.0-2.5 million tonnes of steel a year by the turn of the century. Total domestic demand for steel is about 1.5 million tonnes a year.
